slides: Welcome back, and now a new topic, work and rate.

slides.say: Work questions come up in almost every exam. Workers, machines, pipes and printers all get a job done over time. And one simple formula is behind all of them.
Here it is. Rate times time is equal to work.
at: Rate times time is equal to work

slides.say: The rate is what we do in one unit of time. For example, what we do in one hour.

slides: The time is how long we work. And the work is everything we get done.

slides.say: Let's see it in numbers. A baker makes six cakes an hour, and she works for four hours.
at: A baker makes six cakes an hour

slides.say: So her rate is six cakes an hour, and the time is four hours. Six times four is twenty-four. So her work is twenty-four cakes.
So there are three quantities, the rate, the time and the work. The question gives us two of them, and we find the third.
at: The question gives us two of them

slides.say: If you're not sure when to multiply and when to divide, use the formula triangle.
The work goes on top. The rate and the time go at the bottom, side by side.

slides: Now we cover the one we want. What's left tells us what to do.

slides.say: Cover the work. The rate and the time are left, side by side. So the work is the rate times the time.
at: So the work is the rate times

slides.say: Cover the time. The work is left, over the rate. So the time is the work divided by the rate.
at: So the time is the work divided

slides.say: And cover the rate. The work is left, over the time. So the rate is the work divided by the time.
at: So the rate is the work divided

slides.say: Let's use it. A pump moves thirty liters a minute. How long does it take to move a hundred fifty liters?
They ask for the time. So we cover the time, and the time is the work divided by the rate.
at: the time is the work divided by the rate

slides.say: A hundred fifty divided by thirty is five, because thirty times five is a hundred fifty. So it takes five minutes.
at: A hundred fifty divided by thirty

slides.say: Now the other way. A printer prints forty-eight pages in six minutes. What is its rate?
We cover the rate. The rate is the work divided by the time.
at: The rate is the work divided

slides.say: Forty-eight divided by six is eight. So the printer prints eight pages a minute.
Now careful here, because a lot of students mix up the work and the rate.
A machine fills forty-five bottles in five minutes. What is the work? Forty-five bottles. That's everything it did.
What is the time? Five minutes.
And the rate is the work divided by the time. Forty-five divided by five is nine.
But the rate isn't just nine. It's nine bottles per minute.
Nine bottles is just an amount. Nine bottles per minute is a rate. So a rate always says per what.
at: So a rate always says per what

slides.say: A rate is really a fraction, the work over the time. Forty-five bottles in five minutes is the same rate as nine bottles in one minute.
at: A rate is really a fraction

slides: Both fractions say the same thing. So we can write a rate either way, whichever is easier. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next part.
